sentences.zh: 良玉與民屏馳還，抵家甫一日，而奢崇明黨樊龍反重慶，賫金帛結援。

translations.literal: Liangyu and Minping raced back; they had been home only one day when Fan Long, a follower of She Chongming, rebelled at Chongqing and sent gold and silks to win allies.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Minping raced home, but they had been back only a day when Fan Long, a follower of She Chongming, rebelled at Chongqing and sent gold and silks to win allies.

sentences.zh: 良玉斬其使，即發兵率民屏及邦屏子翼明、拱明溯流西上，度渝城，奄至重慶南坪關，扼賊歸路。

translations.literal: Liangyu executed the envoy, then immediately raised troops and led Minping and Bangping's sons Yiming and Gongming upstream to the west; crossing Yucheng they suddenly arrived at Chongqing's Nanping Pass and blocked the bandits' line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu executed the envoy, then immediately took the field with Minping and Bangping's sons Yiming and Gongming, sailing upstream to the west; crossing Yucheng they suddenly appeared at Chongqing's Nanping Pass and cut off the rebels' retreat.

sentences.zh: 伏兵襲兩河，焚其舟。

translations.literal: Ambush troops struck at Lianghe and burned their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Ambush parties struck at Lianghe and burned the rebel boats.

sentences.zh: 分兵守忠州，馳檄夔州，令急防翟塘上下。

translations.literal: She divided troops to hold Zhongzhou, dispatched urgent orders to Kuizhou, and ordered strict defense above and below Qutang.
translations.idiomatic: She posted troops at Zhongzhou, sent urgent dispatches to Kuizhou, and ordered the garrisons above and below Qutang Gorge to stand on alert.

sentences.zh: 賊出戰，即敗歸。

translations.literal: The bandits came out to fight and were immediately defeated and driven back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out to give battle and were immediately beaten back.

sentences.zh: 良玉上其狀，擢民屏參將，翼明、拱明守備。」

translations.literal: Liangyu submitted a report on the situation; Minping was promoted to Assistant Commander, and Yiming and Gongming to Defending Commanders."
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu reported the situation to the court; Minping was promoted to assistant commander, and Yiming and Gongming to defending commanders."

sentences.zh: 已而奢崇明圍成都急，巡撫朱燮元檄良玉討。

translations.literal: Before long She Chongming pressed the siege of Chengdu urgently; Circuit Intendant Zhu Suiyuan issued orders to Liangyu to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long She Chongming tightened his siege of Chengdu; circuit intendant Zhu Suiyuan ordered Liangyu to march against him.

sentences.zh: 時諸土司皆貪賊賂，逗遛不進。

translations.literal: At the time all the native chieftains were greedy for bandit bribes and lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the native chieftains were all taking rebel bribes and hung back without advancing.

sentences.zh: 獨良玉鼓行而西，收新都，長驅抵成都，賊遂解圍去。

translations.literal: Liangyu alone beat the drums and marched west, recovered Xindu, and drove straight to Chengdu; the bandits then lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu alone pressed forward to the west, retook Xindu, and marched straight on Chengdu; the rebels then lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 良玉乃還軍攻二郎關，民屏先登，已，克佛圖關，復重慶。

translations.literal: Liangyu then turned her army to attack Erlang Pass; Minping was first to scale the wall; before long they took Fotu Pass and recovered Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu then turned her army against Erlang Pass; Minping was first over the wall; soon they took Fotu Pass and recovered Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 良玉初舉兵，即以疏聞。

translations.literal: When Liangyu first raised troops she immediately reported by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangyu first took the field she immediately reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 命封夫人，錫誥命，至是復授都督僉事，充總兵官。

translations.literal: She was ordered ennobled as Lady, granted patent of appointment; at this time she was again granted the post of Commissioner-in-chief and appointed overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: She was ennobled as Lady and granted a patent of appointment; at this point she was also invested as Commissioner-in-chief and appointed overall commander.

sentences.zh: 命祥麟為宜慰使，民屏進副總兵，翼明、拱明進參將。

translations.literal: Xianglin was appointed Pacification Commissioner; Minping was promoted to Deputy Regional Commander; Yiming and Gongming were promoted to Assistant Commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglin was appointed Pacification Commissioner; Minping was promoted to deputy regional commander; Yiming and Gongming were promoted to assistant commanders.

sentences.zh: 良玉益感奮，先後攻克紅崖墩、觀音寺、青山墩諸大巢，蜀賊底定。

translations.literal: Liangyu was all the more stirred to exertion; in succession she stormed the great lairs of Hongyadun, Guanyin Temple, and Qingshandun, and the bandits of Shu were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu fought with renewed zeal; in succession she overran the great rebel bases at Hongyadun, Guanyin Temple, and Qingshandun, and the rebellion in Shu was brought to an end.

sentences.zh: 復以援貴州功，數賚金幣。

translations.literal: Again for merit in aiding Guizhou she was repeatedly granted gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: For her further merit in aiding Guizhou she received repeated grants of gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，良玉上言：「臣率翼明、拱明提兵裹糧，累奏紅崖墩諸捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year Liangyu submitted a memorial: "Your subject led Yiming and Gongming in raising troops and carrying provisions, and repeatedly reported victories at Hongyadun and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year Liangyu memorialized the throne: "I led Yiming and Gongming in raising troops and carrying our own provisions, and repeatedly reported victories at Hongyadun and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 乃行間諸將，未睹賊面，攘臂誇張，及乎對壘，聞風先遁。

translations.literal: Yet the generals along the route, without ever seeing the bandits' faces, flung up their sleeves and boasted extravagantly; when it came to facing the enemy in battle, they fled at the first wind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the generals on the march, who had never even seen the enemy's face, beat their chests and bragged loudly—yet when battle came they fled at the first sign of danger.

sentences.zh: 敗於賊者，唯恐人之勝；

translations.literal: Those defeated by the bandits feared only that others might win;
translations.idiomatic: Those who had lost to the rebels feared nothing so much as someone else winning glory;

sentences.zh: 怯於賊者，唯恐人之強。

translations.literal: those cowardly before the bandits feared only that others might be strong.
translations.idiomatic: those who were cowards before the enemy feared nothing so much as someone else proving strong.

sentences.zh: 如總兵李維新，渡河一戰，敗衄歸營，反閉門拒臣，不容一見。

translations.literal: Such as Overall Commander Li Xinyin, who after one battle crossing the river returned defeated to camp and instead closed his gate and refused your subject, not allowing a single meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Take overall commander Li Xinyin: after one failed crossing of the river he slunk back to camp, then shut his gate against me and refused even to receive me.

sentences.zh: 以六尺軀須眉男子，忌一巾幗婦人，靜夜思之，亦當愧死。

translations.literal: For a six-chi, bearded man to be jealous of a woman in kerchief and hairpins—thinking of it in the quiet of night, he ought to die of shame.
translations.idiomatic: For a full-grown, bearded man to be jealous of a woman in armor—if he reflects on it in the quiet of night, he ought to die of shame.

sentences.zh: 」帝優詔報之，命文武大吏皆以禮待，不得疑忌。

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied with a gracious edict and ordered civil and military grand officials all to treat her with courtesy and not to harbor suspicion or jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied with a gracious edict and ordered civil and military officials at every level to treat her with courtesy and refrain from suspicion or jealousy.

sentences.zh: 是年，民屏從巡撫王三善抵陸廣，兵敗先遁。

translations.literal: That year Minping followed Circuit Intendant Wang San Shan to Luguang; when the army was defeated he fled first.
translations.idiomatic: That year Minping followed circuit intendant Wang San Shan to Luguang and was first to flee when the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 其冬，從戰大方，屢捷。

translations.literal: That winter he followed the campaign at Dafang and repeatedly won victories.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he fought at Dafang and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，退師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊來襲，戰死。

translations.literal: Bandits came to attack and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels attacked on the march and he was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 二子佐明、祚明得脫，皆重傷。

translations.literal: His two sons Zuoming and Zuoming escaped, but both were severely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Zuoming and Zuoming got away, but both were badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 良玉請恤，贈都督同知，立祠賜祭，官二子。

translations.literal: Liangyu requested posthumous honors; he was granted Vice Commissioner-in-chief, a temple was established and sacrificial rites granted, and the two sons were given offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu petitioned for posthumous honors; Minping was invested as Vice Commissioner-in-chief, granted a memorial shrine and sacrificial rites, and both sons were given official posts.

sentences.zh: 而是時翼明、拱明皆進官至副總兵。

translations.literal: By this time Yiming and Gongming had both been promoted to the rank of Deputy Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Yiming and Gongming had both risen to deputy regional commander.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，永平四城失守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen the four cities of Yongping were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen three the four cities of Yongping fell.

sentences.zh: 良玉與翼明奉詔勤王，出家財濟餉。

translations.literal: Liangyu and Yiming received an imperial order to relieve the throne and contributed family wealth to supply rations.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Yiming answered the imperial summons to defend the capital and contributed family wealth to pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝優詔褒美，召見平臺，賜良玉彩幣羊酒，賦四詩旌其功。

translations.literal: Emperor Sizong issued a gracious edict praising them, summoned Liangyu for audience at the review platform, granted her colored silks, sheep, and wine, and composed four poems to honor her merit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Sizong issued a gracious edict of praise, received Liangyu in audience at the review platform, granted her colored silks, sheep, and wine, and composed four poems to honor her achievements.

sentences.zh: 會四城復，乃命良玉歸，而翼明駐近畿。

translations.literal: Just as the four cities were recovered, Liangyu was ordered to return while Yiming was posted near the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When the four cities were recovered Liangyu was ordered home while Yiming was posted near the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年築大淩河城。

translations.literal: The next year Dalinghe City was built.
translations.idiomatic: The following year construction began on Dalinghe City.

sentences.zh: 翼明以萬人護築，城成，命撤兵還鎮。

translations.literal: Yiming guarded the construction with ten thousand men; when the city was completed he was ordered to withdraw his troops and return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yiming guarded the construction with ten thousand men; when the city was finished he was ordered to withdraw and return to his garrison.

sentences.zh: 七年，流賊陷河南，加翼明總兵官，督軍赴討。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when roving bandits took Henan, Yiming was promoted to overall commander and ordered to supervise troops in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when roving rebels overran Henan, Yiming was promoted to overall commander and ordered to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 明年，鄧玘死，以所部皆蜀人，命翼明將之，連破賊於青崖河、吳家堰、袁家坪，扼賊走鄖西路。

translations.literal: The next year Deng Qi died; because his command was entirely Sichuan men, Yiming was ordered to lead them; he repeatedly defeated the bandits at Qingya River, Wujia Weir, and Yuanjiaping, and blocked the bandits' route of flight toward the Yunxi road.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Deng Qi died; since his troops were all Sichuan men, Yiming was ordered to take command of them; he routed the rebels at Qingya River, Wujia Weir, and Yuanjiaping and blocked their escape toward the Yunxi road.

sentences.zh: 翼明性恇怯，部將連敗，不以實聞，革都督銜，貶二秩辦賊。

translations.literal: Yiming was timid and cowardly by nature; his subordinate generals suffered repeated defeats, yet he did not report the truth; his Commissioner-in-chief title was revoked and he was demoted two ranks to serve in bandit suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Yiming was timid by nature; his subordinates suffered repeated defeats, yet he concealed the truth from the court; his Commissioner-in-chief title was stripped and he was demoted two ranks to continue fighting the rebels.

sentences.zh: 已，從盧象升逐賊谷城。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Lu Xiangsheng in driving the bandits at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Lu Xiangsheng in driving the rebels from Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 賊走均州，翼明敗之青石鋪。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Junzhou; Yiming defeated them at Qingshipu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled toward Junzhou, and Yiming defeated them at Qingshipu.

sentences.zh: 賊入山自保，翼明攻破之。

translations.literal: The bandits entered the mountains to defend themselves, and Yiming stormed and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took refuge in the mountains, and Yiming stormed their positions.

sentences.zh: 連破賊界山、三道河、花園溝，擒黑煞神、飛山虎。

translations.literal: In succession he defeated the bandits at Jieshan, Sandao River, and Huayuangou, and captured Heishashen and Feishanhu.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he defeated the rebels at Jieshan, Sandao River, and Huayuangou, capturing the bandit chiefs Heishashen and Feishanhu.

sentences.zh: 賊出沒鄖、襄間，撫治鄖陽苗胙土遣使招降，翼明贊其事，為賊所紿，卒不絳。

translations.literal: The bandits appeared and vanished between Yun and Xiang; Pacification Commissioner of Yunyang Miao Zuotu sent envoys to summon surrender; Yiming supported the effort, but was deceived by the bandits and in the end they did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raided back and forth between Yun and Xiang; Yunyang pacification commissioner Miao Zuotu sent envoys to negotiate surrender; Yiming backed the effort, but the rebels deceived them and in the end never submitted.

sentences.zh: 翼明、胙土皆被劾。

translations.literal: Yiming and Zuotu were both impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Both Yiming and Zuotu were impeached.

sentences.zh: 已而賊犯襄陽，翼明連戰得利，屯兵廟灘，以扼漢江之淺。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits invaded Xiangyang; Yiming fought repeatedly with success, encamped at Miaotan, and blocked the shallow crossing of the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels threatened Xiangyang; Yiming won a series of engagements and encamped at Miaotan to block the shallow fords of the Han River.

sentences.zh: 而羅汝才、劉國能自深水以渡，遂大擾蘄、黃間。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Luo Rucai and Liu Guoneng crossed from deep water and greatly disturbed the region between Qizhou and Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Luo Rucai and Liu Guoneng crossed at the deep fords and threw the region between Qizhou and Huangzhou into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝以鄖、襄屬邑盡殘，罷胙土，切責翼明，尋亦被劾解官。

translations.literal: Because the subordinate districts of Yun and Xiang were all devastated, the Emperor dismissed Zuotu, sharply rebuked Yiming, and soon Yiming was also impeached and removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Because the districts under Yun and Xiang had been laid waste, the emperor dismissed Zuotu, sharply rebuked Yiming, and soon impeached and removed him from office as well.

sentences.zh: 而良玉自京師還，不復援剿，專辦蜀賊。

translations.literal: Liangyu, having returned from the capital, no longer joined relief and suppression campaigns and devoted herself solely to dealing with bandits in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu, having returned from the capital, ceased joining relief campaigns elsewhere and devoted herself exclusively to the bandits in Shu.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，賊陷夔州，圍太平，良玉至乃走。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year the bandits took Kuizhou and besieged Taiping; when Liangyu arrived they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year the rebels seized Kuizhou and besieged Taiping; they withdrew only when Liangyu arrived.

sentences.zh: 十三年扼羅汝才於巫山。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year she blocked Luo Rucai at Wushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year she blocked Luo Rucai at Wushan.

sentences.zh: 汝才犯夔州，良玉師至乃去。

translations.literal: Rucai invaded Kuizhou; when Liangyu's army arrived he departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Rucai attacked Kuizhou, he withdrew only after Liangyu's army arrived.

sentences.zh: 已，邀之馬家寨，斬首六百，追敗之留馬埡，斬其魁東山虎。

translations.literal: Before long she intercepted him at Majia Stockade and beheaded six hundred; pursuing and defeating him at Liuma Pass, she beheaded the chieftain Dongshanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward she intercepted him at Majia Stockade and took six hundred heads; pursuing him to Liuma Pass she routed his force and killed the chieftain Dongshanhu.

sentences.zh: 復合他將大敗之譚家坪北山，又破之仙寺嶺。

translations.literal: Joining other generals she again inflicted a great defeat on him at Beishan in Tanjiaping, and again defeated him at Xiansi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Joining other generals she again shattered his force at Beishan in Tanjiaping and defeated him again at Xiansi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 良玉奪汝才大纛，擒其渠副塌天，賊勢漸衰。

translations.literal: Liangyu seized Rucai's great banner and captured his lieutenant Tiatian; the bandit power gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu captured Rucai's battle standard and seized his lieutenant Tiatian; the rebel power gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 當是時，督師楊嗣昌盡驅賊入川。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Yang Sichang drove all the bandits into Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Secretary Yang Sichang drove all the rebels into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 川撫邵捷春提弱卒二萬守重慶，所倚惟良玉及張令二軍。

translations.literal: Sichuan Circuit Intendant Shao Jiechun led twenty thousand weak soldiers to hold Chongqing; he relied solely on the two armies of Liangyu and Zhang Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan circuit intendant Shao Jiechun held Chongqing with twenty thousand weak troops and relied on no one but the armies of Liangyu and Zhang Ling.

sentences.zh: 綿州知州陸遜之罷官歸，捷春使按營壘。

translations.literal: Mianzhou Prefect Lu Xunzhi, dismissed from office and returning home, was sent by Jiechun to inspect the camps and fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Mianzhou prefect Lu Xunzhi, dismissed from office and on his way home, was sent by Jiechun to inspect the camps and fortifications.

sentences.zh: 見良玉軍整，心異之。

translations.literal: Seeing Liangyu's army in good order, he was struck with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Liangyu's army in excellent order, he was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 良玉為置酒。

translations.literal: Liangyu had wine prepared for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu had wine set out for him.

sentences.zh: 語遜之曰：「邵公不知兵。

translations.literal: She said to Xunzhi: "Lord Shao knows nothing of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: She told Xunzhi: "Lord Shao knows nothing of warfare.

sentences.zh: 吾一婦人，受國恩，誼應死，獨恨與邵公同死耳。

translations.literal: I am but a woman who has received the state's grace; by right I ought to die, and I regret only that I must die together with Lord Shao.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a woman who has received the state's grace; duty demands that I die, and my only regret is that I must die alongside Lord Shao.

sentences.zh: 」遜之問故，良玉曰：「邵公移我自近，去所駐重慶僅三四十里，而遣張令守黃泥窪，殊失地利。

translations.literal: " Xunzhi asked the reason; Liangyu said: "Lord Shao moved me close by, only thirty or forty li from my post at Chongqing, yet sent Zhang Ling to hold Huangniwa—a grave loss of terrain advantage.
translations.idiomatic: " Xunzhi asked why; Liangyu said: "Lord Shao moved me close in, only thirty or forty li from my post at Chongqing, yet posted Zhang Ling at Huangniwa—a grave mistake in terrain.

sentences.zh: 賊據歸、巫萬山巔，俯瞰吾營。

translations.literal: The bandits hold the peaks of the Wan Mountains in Gui and Wu, looking down on our camps.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hold the peaks of the Wan Mountains in Gui and Wu and look down on our camps.

sentences.zh: 鐵騎建瓴下，張令必破。

translations.literal: With iron cavalry pouring down like water from a high pitcher, Zhang Ling is certain to be broken.
translations.idiomatic: With iron cavalry pouring down from above like water off a rooftop, Zhang Ling is sure to be overrun.

sentences.zh: 令破及我，我敗尚能救重慶急乎？

translations.literal: When Ling is broken and the disaster reaches me, if I am defeated can I still relieve Chongqing in its emergency?
translations.idiomatic: Once Ling falls and disaster reaches me, if I am defeated as well, how can I still save Chongqing in its hour of need?

sentences.zh: 且督師以蜀為壑，無愚智知之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Grand Secretary treats Shu as a drainage ditch—there is none, foolish or wise, who does not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, everyone knows the Grand Secretary is using Shu as a ditch to drain the rebellion away.

sentences.zh: 邵公不以此時爭山奪險，令賊無敢即我，而坐以設防，此敗道也。

translations.literal: Lord Shao does not at this time contest the mountains and seize the passes to keep the bandits from approaching us, but instead sits in passive defense—this is the way to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shao fails to seize the heights and passes now, to keep the rebels from closing on us, and instead sits behind fixed defenses—this is the road to defeat.

sentences.zh: 」遜之深然之。

translations.literal: " Xunzhi deeply agreed with her.
translations.idiomatic: " Xunzhi agreed with her completely.

sentences.zh: 已而捷春移營大昌，監軍萬元吉亦進屯巫山，與相應援。

translations.literal: Before long Jiechun shifted his camp to Dachang; Military Overseer Wan Yuanji also advanced and encamped at Wushan, mutually supporting one another.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiechun shifted his camp to Dachang; military overseer Wan Yuanji also advanced to Wushan, and the two forces supported each other.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，張獻忠連破官軍於觀音巖、三黃嶺，遂從上馬渡過軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Zhang Xianzhong repeatedly defeated the government army at Guanyin Cliff and Sanhuang Ridge, then crossed the army at Shangmadu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Zhang Xianzhong routed government forces at Guanyin Cliff and Sanhuang Ridge, then crossed the river at Shangmadu.

sentences.zh: 良玉偕張令急扼之竹{}坪，挫其鋒。

translations.literal: Liangyu together with Zhang Ling hurriedly blocked him at Zhujun Ping and blunted his momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu and Zhang Ling hurried to block him at Zhujun Ping and blunted his advance.

sentences.zh: 會令為賊所殪，良玉趨救不克，轉鬥復敗，所部三萬人略盡。

translations.literal: Just then Ling was killed by the bandits; Liangyu rushed to rescue but could not succeed, turned to fight and was again defeated, and her force of thirty thousand was nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ling was killed by the rebels; Liangyu rushed to his rescue but failed, turned to fight and was beaten again, and her force of thirty thousand was nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 乃單騎見捷春請曰：「事急矣，盡發吾溪峒卒，可得二萬。

translations.literal: She then went alone on horseback to see Jiechun and pleaded: "The situation is urgent; if all my stream-gorge troops are mobilized, twenty thousand can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: She then rode alone to see Jiechun and pleaded: "The situation is desperate. Mobilize all my stream-and-gorge troops and I can raise twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 我自廩其半，半餼之官，猶足辦賊。

translations.literal: I myself will supply rations for half of them from my own stores, and half will be supplied by the government—still enough to deal with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: I will feed half from my own stores and the government can supply the other half—enough still to finish the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」捷春見嗣昌與己左，而倉無見糧，謝其計不用。

translations.literal: " Jiechun saw that Sichang was at odds with him, and the granary had no ready grain; he declined the plan and did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiechun, seeing that Sichang was hostile to him and that the granary held no ready grain, declined the plan.

sentences.zh: 良玉乃嘆息歸。

translations.literal: Liangyu then sighed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu sighed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時搖、黃十三家賊橫蜀中。

translations.literal: At the time the thirteen bandit clans of Yao and Huang ran rampant in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the thirteen Yao and Huang bandit clans ran rampant across Shu.

sentences.zh: 有秦纘勛者，良玉族人也，為賊耳目，被擒，殺獄卒遁去。

translations.literal: There was one Qin Zuanxun, a clansman of Liangyu, who served as the bandits' eyes and ears; he was captured, killed a prison guard, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: One Qin Zuanxun, a kinsman of Liangyu, served as a rebel spy; captured, he killed a jailer and escaped.

sentences.zh: 良玉捕執以獻，無脫者。

translations.literal: Liangyu captured and seized him and presented him; none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu captured him and turned him over; none escaped her net.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠盡陷楚地，將復入蜀。

translations.literal: Zhang Xianzhong had taken all the Chu territories and was about to enter Shu again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong had overrun the Chu territories and was preparing to invade Shu again.

sentences.zh: 良玉圖全蜀形勢上之巡撫陳士奇，請益兵守十三隘，士奇不能用。

translations.literal: Liangyu drew a map of the overall situation in Shu and submitted it to Circuit Intendant Chen Shiji, requesting additional troops to hold the thirteen passes; Shiji could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu mapped the overall situation in Shu and submitted it to circuit intendant Chen Shiji, requesting reinforcements to hold the thirteen passes; Shiji would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 復上之巡按劉之勃，之勃許之，而無兵可發。

translations.literal: She again submitted it to Surveillance Commissioner Liu Zhibo; Zhibo agreed, but there were no troops to dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: She submitted it again to surveillance commissioner Liu Zhibo; Zhibo agreed, but no troops could be spared.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，獻忠遂長驅犯夔州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year Xianzhong then drove straight in and invaded Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year Xianzhong marched straight in and attacked Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 良玉馳援，眾寡不敵，潰。

translations.literal: Liangyu raced to relieve it; outnumbered, she collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu rushed to the rescue but was heavily outnumbered and her force broke.

sentences.zh: 及全蜀盡陷，良玉慷慨語其眾曰：「吾兄弟二人皆死王事，吾以一孱婦蒙國恩二十年，今不幸至此，其敢以余年事逆賊哉！

translations.literal: When all Shu was lost, Liangyu spoke passionately to her troops, saying: "My two brothers both died in the king's service; I, a frail woman, have received the state's grace for twenty years. Now that misfortune has brought us here, how could I dare spend my remaining years serving the rebel bandits!
translations.idiomatic: When all Shu had fallen, Liangyu spoke passionately to her troops: "Both my brothers died in the state's service. I, a frail woman, have enjoyed the state's grace for twenty years. Now that fortune has brought us to this pass, how could I spend my remaining years serving rebels!

sentences.zh: 」悉召所部約曰：「有從賊者，族無赦！

translations.literal: " She summoned all her command and pledged: "Whoever follows the bandits—his clan shall not be spared!
translations.idiomatic: " She summoned her entire command and declared: "Anyone who joins the rebels—his whole clan will be put to death!

sentences.zh: 」乃分兵守四境。

translations.literal: " She then divided troops to guard the four borders.
translations.idiomatic: " She then posted troops to guard every border.

sentences.zh: 賊遍招土司，獨無敢至石砫者。

translations.literal: The bandits summoned native chieftains everywhere, but none dared come to Shizhu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels summoned native chieftains everywhere, yet none dared approach Shizhu.

sentences.zh: 後獻忠死，良玉竟以壽終。

translations.literal: Later, after Xianzhong died, Liangyu in the end died of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Xianzhong's death, Liangyu lived out her years and died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 翼明既罷，崇禎十六年冬，起四川總兵官。

translations.literal: After Yiming was dismissed, in the winter of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Overall Commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yiming was dismissed, he was recalled in the winter of Chongzhen sixteen as overall commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 道梗，命不達。

translations.literal: The roads were blocked and the order did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were blocked and the order never reached him.

sentences.zh: 而拱明值普名聲之亂，與賊鬥死，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: Gongming, encountering the turmoil of Pu Mingsheng, fought the bandits and died; posthumous honors and relief were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Gongming, caught up in Pu Mingsheng's rebellion, fought the rebels and was killed; he received posthumous honors and relief according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 龍在田，石屏州土官舍人也。

translations.literal: Long Zaitian was a native official's retainer of Shiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Long Zaitian was a retainer of the native official of Shiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，雲南賊安效良、張世臣等為亂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi the Yunnan bandits An Xiaoliang, Zhang Shichen, and others raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi two the Yunnan rebels An Xiaoliang, Zhang Shichen, and others rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 在田與阿迷普名聲、武定吾必奎等征討，數有功，得為土守備。

translations.literal: Zaitian together with Pu Mingsheng of Ami, Wu BiKui of Wuding, and others campaigned in suppression; he achieved merit repeatedly and was made Native Defending Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zaitian campaigned with Pu Mingsheng of Ami, Wu BiKui of Wuding, and others, won repeated victories, and was appointed native defending commander.

sentences.zh: 新平賊剽石屏，安效良攻沾益，在田俱破走之。

translations.literal: Bandits from Xinping raided Shiping; An Xiaoliang attacked Zhanyi; Zaitian in both cases defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits from Xinping raided Shiping and An Xiaoliang attacked Zhanyi, Zaitian defeated and drove off both forces.

sentences.zh: 巡撫閔洪學上其功，擢坐營都司。

translations.literal: Circuit Intendant Min Hongxue submitted a report on his merit, and he was promoted to Camp Director.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendant Min Hongxue reported his merits, and he was promoted to camp director.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年與必奎收復烏撒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he together with BiKui recovered Wusa.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen two he and BiKui recovered Wusa.

sentences.zh: 八年，流賊犯鳳陽，詔征雲南土兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when roving bandits invaded Fengyang, an imperial order summoned Yunnan native troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when roving rebels attacked Fengyang, an imperial order summoned Yunnan native troops.

sentences.zh: 在田率所部應詔，擊賊湖廣、河南，頻有功，擢副總兵。

translations.literal: Zaitian led his command in response to the edict, attacked bandits in Huguang and Henan, repeatedly achieved merit, and was promoted to Deputy Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zaitian answered the summons with his command, fought rebels in Huguang and Henan, won repeated victories, and was promoted to deputy regional commander.

sentences.zh: 總理盧象升檄討襄陽賊，至則象升已奉詔勤王，命屬熊文燦。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng issued orders to suppress the Xiangyang bandits; when Zaitian arrived Xiangsheng had already received an imperial order to relieve the throne, and he was placed under Xiong Wencan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Lu Xiangsheng ordered him to suppress the Xiangyang rebels; when he arrived Xiangsheng had already been summoned to defend the capital, and he was placed under Xiong Wencan.

sentences.zh: 十年三月擊擒大盜郭三海。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year he attacked and captured the great bandit Guo Sanhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year he captured the great bandit Guo Sanhai.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月大破賀一龍、李萬慶於雙溝，進都督同知。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he inflicted a great defeat on He Yilong and Li Wanqing at Shuang Gou and was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he routed He Yilong and Li Wanqing at Shuang Gou and was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年三月大破賊固始，斬首三千五百有奇。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year he inflicted a great defeat on the bandits at Gushi, beheading more than thirty-five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year he routed the rebels at Gushi, taking more than thirty-five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 張獻忠之叛也，文燦命在田駐谷城，遏賊東突。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xianzhong rebelled, Wencan ordered Zaitian to garrison Gucheng and block the bandits' breakout to the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xianzhong rebelled, Wencan ordered Zaitian to garrison Gucheng and block any breakout to the east.

sentences.zh: 諸將多忌在田，讒言日興。

translations.literal: Many generals were jealous of Zaitian, and slanderous talk arose daily.
translations.idiomatic: Many generals envied Zaitian, and slander against him mounted daily.

sentences.zh: 及文燦被逮，在田亦罷歸，還至貴州，擊平叛賊安隴壁。

translations.literal: When Wencan was arrested, Zaitian was also dismissed and returned home; reaching Guizhou, he attacked and pacified the rebel An Longbi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencan was arrested, Zaitian was dismissed and sent home; back in Guizhou he suppressed the rebel An Longbi.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏，中原盜益熾。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year, banditry in the Central Plain grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifteenth year rebellion in the Central Plain burned hotter still.

sentences.zh: 在田上疏曰：「臣以石屏世弁，因流氛震陵，奮激國難，捐貲募精卒九千五百，戰象四，戰馬二千，入楚、豫破賊。

translations.literal: Zaitian submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject, a hereditary retainer of Shiping, stirred by the roving turmoil that shook the imperial tombs, roused himself in the nation's crisis, contributed his wealth to recruit nine thousand five hundred picked soldiers, four war elephants, and two thousand war horses, and entered Chu and Yu to defeat the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zaitian memorialized the throne: "I am a hereditary retainer of Shiping. When the roving rebels shook the imperial tombs I roused myself in the nation's crisis, spent my own wealth to raise nine thousand five hundred picked soldiers, four war elephants, and two thousand war horses, and marched into Chu and Yu to defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊不敢窺江北陵寢，滇兵有力焉。

translations.literal: The bandits did not dare look toward the imperial tombs north of the Yangtze; the Yunnan troops had strength in this.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not dare threaten the imperial tombs north of the Yangtze—and the Yunnan troops had much to do with that.

sentences.zh: 五載捷二十有八，忌口中阻，逼臣病歸。

translations.literal: In five years there were twenty-eight victories, but jealous tongues obstructed me and forced your subject home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In five years I won twenty-eight victories, but jealous tongues blocked my path and forced me home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 自臣罷，親藩辱，名城屢陷。

translations.literal: Since your subject was dismissed, imperial clansmen have been shamed and famous cities repeatedly fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Since my dismissal, imperial princes have been humiliated and famous cities have fallen again and again.

sentences.zh: 臣妄謂討寇必須南兵。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that suppressing bandits requires southern troops.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that suppressing the rebels requires southern troops.

sentences.zh: 蓋諸將所統多烏合，遇寇即逃，乏餉即噪。

translations.literal: For the generals mostly command motley gatherings—when they meet bandits they flee; when rations run short they mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: The generals mostly command motley rabbles—when they meet rebels they flee; when pay runs short they mutiny.

sentences.zh: 滇兵萬里長驅，家人父子同誌，非若他軍易潰也。

translations.literal: Yunnan troops march ten thousand li; fathers and sons share one purpose—they are not like other armies that break easily.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan troops march ten thousand li from home; fathers and sons fight with one purpose—they do not break like other armies.

sentences.zh: 且一歲中，秋冬氣涼，賊得馳騁。

translations.literal: Moreover, within a year, in autumn and winter when the air is cool, the bandits can ride and range freely.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in autumn and winter when the air turns cool, the rebels can ride and raid at will.

sentences.zh: 春夏即入山避暑，養銳而出，故其氣益盛。

translations.literal: In spring and summer they enter the mountains to escape the heat, recover their edge, and emerge again—thus their momentum grows ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer they retreat into the mountains to escape the heat, recover their strength, and emerge again—so their momentum only grows.

sentences.zh: 夫平原戰既不勝，山蹊又莫敢攖，師老財殫，蕩平何日。

translations.literal: If they cannot win on the plains and dare not grapple on mountain paths, with the army worn and funds exhausted—on what day will pacification come?
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot win on the plains and dare not fight in the mountains, with armies exhausted and treasuries drained—when will the realm ever be pacified?

sentences.zh: 滇兵輕走遠跳，善搜山。

translations.literal: Yunnan troops move lightly, leap far, and are skilled at searching the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan troops are light on their feet, cover great distances, and excel at mountain sweeps.

sentences.zh: 臣願整萬眾，力掃秦、楚、豫、皖諸寇，不滅不止。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to marshal ten thousand men and sweep with force the bandits of Qin, Chu, Yu, and Wan, not stopping until they are exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to marshal ten thousand men and sweep the rebels from Qin, Chu, Yu, and Wan—I will not stop until they are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 望速給行糧，沿途接濟。

translations.literal: I hope marching rations may be quickly supplied and relief provided along the route.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that marching rations be supplied promptly and relief provided along the route.

sentences.zh: 臣誓捐軀報國，言而不效，甘伏斧钅質。

translations.literal: Your subject vows to give his body in service to the state; if my words prove ineffective, I am willing to submit to the executioner's axe.
translations.idiomatic: I swear to give my life for the state; if my words prove empty, I am willing to submit to the executioner's block.

sentences.zh: 」帝壯之，下兵部議，寢不行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was impressed by him and referred the matter to the Ministry of War for deliberation, but it was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was moved by his words and referred the matter to the Ministry of War, but the proposal was shelved and never enacted.

sentences.zh: 逾二載，乙酉八月，吾必奎叛。

translations.literal: More than two years later, in the eighth month of the yiyou year, Wu BiKui rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: More than two years later, in the eighth month of the yiyou year, Wu BiKui rebelled.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐天波檄在田及寧州土知州祿永命協討，擊擒之。

translations.literal: Duke of Qian Mu Tianbo issued orders to Zaitian and Ningzhou Native Prefect Lu Yongming to join in suppression; they attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Qian Mu Tianbo ordered Zaitian and Ningzhou native prefect Lu Yongming to join the suppression; they attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，沙定洲作亂，據雲南府，在田不敢擊。

translations.literal: Before long Sha Dingzhou raised rebellion, seized Yunnan Prefecture, and Zaitian did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sha Dingzhou rebelled, seized Yunnan Prefecture, and Zaitian did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 明年，定州攻在田不下，移攻寧州，尋陷習峨，在田走大理。

translations.literal: The next year Dingzhou attacked Zaitian but could not take him; he shifted to attack Ningzhou, soon took Xi'e, and Zaitian fled to Dali.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Dingzhou attacked Zaitian but failed to take him; he turned on Ningzhou, soon seized Xi'e, and Zaitian fled to Dali.

sentences.zh: 又明年，孫可望等至貴州，在田說令攻定洲，定洲迄破滅。

translations.literal: The year after that, Sun Kewang and others reached Guizhou; Zaitian persuaded them to attack Dingzhou, and Dingzhou was in the end destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that Sun Kewang and others reached Guizhou; Zaitian persuaded them to attack Dingzhou, and Dingzhou was finally destroyed.

sentences.zh: 在田歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Zaitian returned home and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Zaitian returned home and died there.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：馬世龍等值邊陲多事，奮其勇略，著績戎行，或捐軀力戰，身膏原野，可謂無忝爪牙之任矣。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Ma Shilong and the others lived in times when the frontiers were troubled; they exerted their courage and strategy and achieved distinction in military service; some gave their bodies and fought with all their strength, their flesh enriching the wild fields—they can be said not to have disgraced the charge of the state's claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Ma Shilong and his fellows served when the frontiers were in turmoil; they exerted their courage and strategy and won distinction in the field. Some gave their lives in fierce combat and enriched the wilderness with their blood—they did not disgrace the trust placed in the state's sword-arm.

sentences.zh: 夫摧鋒陷敵，宿將猶難，而秦良玉一土舍婦人，提兵裹糧，崎嶇轉鬥，其急公赴義有足多者。

translations.literal: To break the enemy vanguard and plunge into the foe—even veteran generals find this difficult; yet Qin Liangyu, a woman of a native-official household, led troops carrying their own rations and fought through rugged terrain in repeated battles; her urgency in public duty and rush to righteousness deserve much praise.
translations.idiomatic: To break the enemy vanguard and plunge into battle is hard even for veteran generals—yet Qin Liangyu, a woman from a native-official household, led troops carrying their own provisions and fought through rugged country in battle after battle. Her zeal for the public good and rush to righteous action deserve the highest praise.

sentences.zh: 彼仗鉞臨戎，縮朒觀望者，視此能無愧乎！

translations.literal: Those who bearing axes command armies yet shrink back and watch from the sidelines—can they look on this without shame!
translations.idiomatic: Those who held command yet shrank back to watch from the sidelines—can they look on her example without shame!
